label: model_selection_iter1
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 1: move the ranking axis by swapping the linear baseline for a gradient-boosted tree ensemble that can capture the non-linear, interaction-heavy structure of the speed-dating features (like / attractive_partner / guess_prob_liked vs. the stated-preference and activity columns), and let it split on NaN itself instead of median-imputing 60 partially-missing columns. Fit a single hist_gbdt on all 5,026 training rows with impute: none, no scaling, moderate capacity and mild L2, and class_weight='balanced' so the default predict() cut lands near the balanced point rather than deep in the majority class. Read roc_auc / pr_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against the baseline's 0.8419 / 0.5751 / 0.7649 to see how far the ranking actually moved, and cut_headroom to see whether any residual gap is operating point or ranking; that decides whether attempt 2 tunes capacity (ranking) or the class weight ratio (cut).",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "hist_gbdt",
    "xgboost",
    "random_forest"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "max_iter": 400,
    "learning_rate": 0.06,
    "max_leaf_nodes": 31,
    "l2_regularization": 1.0,
    "class_weight": "balanced",
    "early_stopping": false
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "none",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "No previous attempt. Relative to the card's baseline (logreg + median impute + standard scale): different family (hist_gbdt instead of linear), no imputation (native NaN splits) and no scaling, 400 boosting iterations at lr 0.06 with 31 leaves and l2=1.0, and class_weight='balanced' to shift the default cut.",
  "rationale": "The goal bar 0.8882 sits above the baseline ranking's ceiling (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7649, KS 0.5297), so no threshold or weight setting inside the linear family can reach it — the ranking itself has to improve, which means a different family or more information in the columns. hist_gbdt is the strongest single estimator available for 119 mixed tabular columns at 8.4k rows and is the family most likely to add ranking power over a linear model on features whose signal is interaction-shaped (partner ratings crossed with stated preferences, gender, wave). impute: none is available only to hist_gbdt<path> and lets the tree treat 'not measured' as its own branch on the 60 columns with missing values (one at 78.5% missing) instead of collapsing them onto a median; missing_indicator is documented as bit-for-bit redundant under impute: none, and missing_count bought nothing, so neither is requested. Scaling is irrelevant to trees. early_stopping is explicitly false because at 5,026 training rows the auto setting is off anyway and asking for it would cost 503 rows and make the score non-comparable; instead capacity is controlled by lr 0.06 with l2=1.0 and 31 leaves, which is a conservative point for this row count. class_weight='balanced' addresses the 5.07:1 imbalance on the operating-point axis — the baseline's recall 0.4022 against high specificity shows the default cut is far into the majority class — while the ranking metrics reported alongside will tell me how much of any gain was ranking versus cut, so the next attempt can be aimed at the axis that is actually short. Cost 3 with 400 iterations on 5k rows is comfortably inside 600 s and 2 GB.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 1
}
